methodology.purpose: Small, dated, provenance-first signals that complement the undated historical targeting dataset.
methodology.datePolicy: publishedAt is the source publication date. observedAt is null unless the source gives a defensible observation date for the claim. A source update date is metadata, not an incident date.
methodology.matchingPolicy: Sector and country claims are independent dimensions. Do not infer that an entity targeted the selected sector in the selected country unless intersectionStatus is confirmed.
methodology.freshnessPolicy: A recent publication or catalogue update is evidence recency, not proof that an intrusion is currently under way.

evidenceTiers.vendor-observed: A named threat-intelligence provider describes activity it directly observed.
evidenceTiers.law-enforcement-assessed: A law-enforcement authority reports an investigative or disruption assessment.
evidenceTiers.government-warning: A government authority publishes a warning or defensive notice.
evidenceTiers.authoritative-catalogue: An authoritative catalogue consolidates referenced public reporting and preserves entity classification.

sectorClaims.claim: Google Threat Intelligence Group lists financial services among the sectors on which UNC3944 has had a notable focus and reports a financial-services targeting wave in late 2023.

countryClaims.claim: Google Threat Intelligence Group lists the United Kingdom among the English-speaking countries in UNC3944's primary geographical focus.

signals.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group describes UNC3944, which overlaps with public reporting on Scattered Spider, as a financially motivated actor with broad sector and English-speaking-country targeting patterns.

source.name: Google Threat Intelligence Group / Mandiant — Defending Against UNC3944

caveats: The source's sector and country lists are aggregate patterns and do not establish a confirmed UK financial-services victim.
The publication noted a decline in activity after 2024 law-enforcement action; a later NCA disruption assessment is represented as a separate signal.

countryClaims.claim: The UK National Crime Agency reports that action against two leading members severely disrupted the Scattered Spider threat.

signals.summary: The UK National Crime Agency says arrests and convictions effectively halted the group's criminal activity and cites an independent Microsoft assessment that the arrests materially degraded its operational ability.

source.name: UK National Crime Agency — Two sentenced for hacking Transport for London

caveats: The NCA warns that other cybercriminals may continue to use the damaged Scattered Spider brand.
This is an operational-status signal, not evidence of current targeting of the financial-services sector.

sectorClaims.claim: The FBI says ShinyHunters targets major companies across technology, finance and retail.

signals.summary: An FBI public-service announcement describes ShinyHunters as a cybercriminal group specialising in large-scale data breaches and extortion and identifies finance as one of its target sectors.

source.name: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center — ShinyHunters public-service announcement

caveats: The FBI notice does not identify a confirmed UK financial-services victim.
The FBI cautions that threat actors may make real or exaggerated claims about access or stolen information.
ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider are separate ATT&CK groups; association with a broader criminal community does not make them aliases.

sectorClaims.claim: MITRE ATT&CK lists financial services among the primary sectors in aggregate reporting on Qilin affiliate victims.

countryClaims.claim: MITRE ATT&CK lists the United Kingdom among the countries containing the majority of victims in aggregate reporting on Qilin affiliates.

signals.summary: MITRE ATT&CK classifies Qilin as malware: a ransomware family operated as ransomware-as-a-service, with affiliates responsible for victim targeting.
caveats: Qilin is ransomware used through a ransomware-as-a-service model, not a threat-actor identity.
The sector and country lists are aggregate dimensions and do not establish a confirmed UK financial-services victim.
The ATT&CK last-modified date records catalogue maintenance, not the date of an intrusion.
